tools.name: search_providers
tools.description: Find residential emergency plumbers or electricians in Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area (urgent, unplanned work such as burst pipes, sewer backups, no power, tripped panels; not renovations). Read-only; no side effects beyond request logging. Needs trade plus location or postal_code. Returns up

tools.name: get_provider
tools.description: Get full details for one provider by id (from search_providers): full weekly hours, fees, all service areas, all contact channels, licences, review sources, last_verified. Read-only. Not needed to answer a normal search: search_providers results already include phone, availability, fees, licence and

tools.name: report_contact
tools.description: WRITE (stores one record; not destructive). Records the outcome of a contact attempt the user actually made, so availability data stays accurate. Only call when the user has contacted the provider and agrees to share the outcome. Never include personal details about the customer.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_providers, get_provider · Private data: search_providers, get_provider, report_contact · Public sink: search_providers, get_provider, report_contact.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_providers, get_provider · Private data: search_providers, get_provider, report_contact · Public sink: search_providers, get_provider, report_contact

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
